title: Šibenik Prices and Realistic 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: What Šibenik costs now and what to budget in 2027: daily budgets, Krka and fortress tickets, food, transport and ways to save, all in euros.
content:
## How Much Does Šibenik Cost in 2027?

Šibenik is moderately priced by Croatian standards. It costs less than Dubrovnik and Split, and a bit more than it did before the 2023 euro changeover. Published traveler-spending averages put a mid-range day at about €115 per person, with budget travelers near €50 and luxury travelers near €220. Those averages include shared-room accommodation, food, local transport and sights.

The 2027 numbers below are projections built from 2026 prices plus a modest rise. Expect roughly 3-6% on restaurants and accommodation, which is in line with recent Croatian inflation in tourism. Some 2027 rates, including the St Nicholas Fortress boat season, were not yet announced at the time of writing.

## How Have Prices Changed Recently?

- **Accommodation** moves the most. Summer rates for private rooms and apartments sit well above shoulder-season rates, and the gap is widening each year.
- **Restaurants** have risen steadily since the euro changeover. A konoba lunch now runs €10-18, and dinner with a drink €20-40.
- **Drinks** are stable. Coffee or a local beer costs €2.50-4.
- **Krka National Park** uses a fixed three-tier seasonal scale: €7 in winter, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. Treat any 2027 change as a possibility, but the same structure is listed for 2027.
- **Local transport** stays cheap. City buses cost €1.50-2.50 per ride.

Šibenik still costs less than the better-known Dalmatian coastal towns, mainly because it has fewer cruise crowds and less tourism infrastructure.

## Realistic 2027 Daily Budgets Per Person

### Tight budget: €60-80 per day
This covers a hostel dorm or a basic private room, bakery breakfasts, one konoba lunch, self-catered dinners and free sights. Walking the Old Town, the waterfront and the cathedral exterior costs nothing.

### Mid-range: €110-150 per day
This covers a 3-star hotel or a good apartment shared by two, a konoba lunch and dinner, coffees, and one paid attraction a day. A three-day trip including one Krka day typically lands at €450-650 per person in this tier, excluding flights.

### Comfortable or luxury: €220 and up per day
This covers a boutique or four-star stay, tasting-menu dinners, Babić wine, and private boat or Kornati excursions. A guided private tour can reach €400 or more per day.

### Budget for a couple
A couple on a mid-range plan should allow about €1,700-2,400 for a week in shoulder season, excluding flights, and €2,400-3,400 in July and August.

## Accommodation Costs

Private rooms and apartments run roughly €45-90 per night in the shoulder season. Mid-range hotels and good apartments rise to €100-170 in July and August. Hostel beds cost about €25-35. Book summer 2027 stays by early spring, since the best Old Town apartments go first.

Staying in the Old Town costs more than staying 1-2 km out, but the whole center is walkable. The Old Town has steps and cobbles, so check luggage access before booking.

## Food and Drink Prices

| Item | Typical 2027 price |
|---|---|
| Bakery breakfast | €3-6 |
| Konoba lunch | €10-18 |
| Konoba dinner with a drink | €20-40 |
| Coffee | €2-3 |
| Local beer | €3-4.50 |
| Glass of Babić red wine | €4-6 |

The waterfront restaurants charge the most. Walk two or three streets into the Old Town for the same dishes at lower prices. Typical local dishes include Skradin risotto, grilled fish by weight, and peka. Fish by weight is where bills jump, so ask the price per kilogram before ordering.

A daily food budget of €45-55 covers a lunch, a dinner with a drink and coffees.

## Sights and Activities

### Krka National Park
Krka is about 15 km from the city. Adult tickets cost €40 from June to September, €30 after 15:00 in peak months, €20 in April, May and October, and €7 from November to March. Children aged 7-18 pay €15 in summer, and children under 7 enter free. The ticket includes the Skradin boat and the Lozovac bus from April to October. Boat trips to Visovac and Roški slap cost extra.

Swimming below Skradinski buk is banned, so do not plan a swim there.

### St Nicholas Fortress
The UNESCO fortress is reached by official boat from the Krka berth on the Šibenik waterfront. An adult ticket costs €21, ages 7-18 pay €16, and children under 7 are free. The trip takes about 2 hours, with 50 minutes sailing and an hour on site. There are up to four departures a day. The 2026 season ran from 5 May to 18 October, and 2027 dates were not published yet. It closes in winter.

This is the one tour in town that is priced above its value right now. Skip the fortress if your time is short or your budget tight, and spend the money on a Krka day instead. The channel views are good, but the fortress itself is still being renovated.

### Old Town fortresses
St Michael's Fortress and Barone Fortress are in the city. A combined fortress ticket runs about €10-15, depending on which fortresses and the season. Present a Krka, Kornati or fortress ticket for a 10% discount on the St Nicholas boat. The Šibenik Card gives 20%.

### St James Cathedral
The cathedral is UNESCO-listed (2000). The entry fee is small, typically a few euros, and it is the best-value paid sight in town.

## Getting There and Around

- **City buses:** €1.50-2.50 per ride.
- **Bus to Skradin:** about €3-5 one way.
- **Rental car:** roughly €25-35 per day outside peak season, higher in July and August.
- **From Split:** bus and local transfer cost about €14-20 per person.
- **Taxis** cost more than a rental car on multi-day trips, so use them only for short airport or late-night rides.

You do not need a car inside the city. A car helps only for Krka's Lozovac entrance, Primošten or Kornati departures.

## Cheapest and Most Expensive Times

- **Cheapest:** November to March. Krka is €7, two fortresses stay open at no or low cost, and rooms are the lowest of the year. St Nicholas is closed.
- **Best value:** May, early June, September and early October. Krka is €20 or €40 in early summer, the St Nicholas boats run, and the sea is warm in September.
- **Most expensive:** July and August, with the highest room prices and the €40 Krka ticket.

## Money-Saving Tips for 2027

- Visit Krka in April, May or October for €20 instead of €40. The saving is €20 per person.
- In peak months, arrive after 15:00 for the €30 ticket, or enter via Skradin to use the included boat.
- Buy a Šibenik Card for the 20% fortress-boat discount if visiting several sights.
- Eat lunch as the main meal. Many konobas offer a cheaper daily set menu.
- Fill bottles from tap water, which is safe to drink.
- Book ahead for July and August, when apartments often sell out first.

## Sample 3-Day Budget Per Person (2027)

| Style | 3 days | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| Tight | €250-350 | Hostel or basic room, simple meals, one Krka day in shoulder season |
| Mid-range | €450-650 | Hotel or apartment, konoba meals, Krka, fortress |
| Comfortable | €800-1,200 | Boutique stay, good dining, private excursions |

These figures exclude flights and large alcohol spending.

faq.question: How much does a trip to Šibenik cost per day in 2027?
faq.answer: Plan on about €60-80 per person on a tight budget, €110-150 mid-range, and €220 or more for luxury. Summer accommodation is the largest variable. Shoulder months bring the same trip down noticeably.

faq.question: Is Šibenik cheaper than Split or Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Yes, slightly. Average traveler spending in Šibenik is about €115 a day, against about €121 in Dubrovnik. The difference is larger for accommodation and restaurant prices in the Old Town.

faq.question: How much is a Krka National Park ticket in 2027?
faq.answer: The current structure is €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. After 15:00 in peak months the adult ticket is €30. The ticket includes the Skradin boat and Lozovac bus from April to October.

faq.question: Is St Nicholas Fortress worth €21?
faq.answer: It is worth it if you want the UNESCO listing and the St Anthony Channel sail. The trip takes about 2 hours and the fortress is still under renovation, so budget travelers can skip it. Boats run only in season, and 2027 dates were not yet confirmed.

faq.question: What is the cheapest month to visit Šibenik?
faq.answer: January and February are cheapest, with Krka at €7 and low room rates. The trade-off is that St Nicholas is closed and some seasonal restaurants shut. For good weather at lower cost, choose May or late September.

faq.question: How much should I budget for food in Šibenik?
faq.answer: Allow €45-55 per person per day. A konoba lunch is €10-18, dinner with a drink is €20-40, and coffee or beer is €2.50-4. Eating away from the waterfront lowers the bill.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Šibenik?
faq.answer: No, the Old Town and waterfront are walkable, and city buses cost €1.50-2.50. A car is useful only for Krka's Lozovac entrance and coastal day trips. Buses to Skradin cost about €3-5 one way.

quickAnswer: Plan on €60-80 per person per day on a tight budget, €110-150 mid-range, and €220 or more for luxury in Šibenik in 2027. Peak summer lifts accommodation the most. Krka costs €7-40 depending on the month, and St Nicholas Fortress is €21. Shoulder months are the best value.
